records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֞א הַגּוֹרָ֤ל הַשֵּׁנִי֙ לְשִׁמְע֔וֹן לְמַטֵּ֥ה בְנֵֽי־שִׁמְע֖וֹן לְמִשְׁפְּחוֹתָ֑ם וַֽיְהִי֙ נַֽחֲלָתָ֔ם בְּת֖וֹךְ נַחֲלַ֥ת בְּנֵֽי־יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And came out the lot the second for Simeon, for [the] tribe of [the] sons of Simeon by their clans; and was their inheritance in [the] midst of [the] inheritance of [the] sons of Judah.
pieces: The second lot came out for the tribe of Simeon, clan by clan. Their inheritance lay inside the inheritance of the tribe of Judah.

L.1: And the second lot came out for Simeon, for the tribe of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Simeon by their clans, and their inheritance was in the midst of the inheritance of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah.

R.1: The second lot was drawn for the tribe of Simeon, clan by clan. Their share of land was inside the land of the tribe of Judah.

decisions.choice: the second lot: the second of the seven lots cast at Shiloh
decisions.reason: Joshua had men survey the land still to be divided and write it down in seven parts, and then he cast lots for them before the LORD at Shiloh (18:1-10). The first lot fell to Benjamin (18:11). Casting lots left the choice to God (Proverbs 16:33), so each tribe received its land as his gift and not by its own claim. This chapter gives the other six lots in turn.

decisions.choice: in the midst of the inheritance of Judah: Simeon has no region of its own
decisions.reason: Simeon's towns lie inside the southern part of Judah's land, and most of them already appear in Judah's list (15:26-32, 42). Verse 9 gives the reason. Behind it stands Jacob's word about Simeon and Levi: "I will divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel" (Genesis 49:7).

decisions.choice: inheritance: land given to a family as a lasting possession
decisions.reason: The word names property that passes down within a family from one generation to the next. Israel's land was divided among tribes, clans and families as a gift from God that was to stay in the family (Numbers 26:52-56; 27:1-11). It was received, not earned or bought.

decisions.choice: the tribe of Simeon, clan by clan
alternatives: the tribe of the descendants of Simeon
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the tribe of the sons of Simeon by their clans". Literal keeps "sons" with the gender setting, since the tribe was its men, women and children. Balanced and Readable say "the tribe of Simeon", since "sons of Simeon" is simply the tribe's name, and "clan by clan", since the land was shared out among the clans within the tribe. The same wording is used for every tribe in this chapter.

decisions.choice: the lot was drawn; share of land
decisions.reason: Readable says the lot "was drawn" and calls the inheritance a "share of land", which young readers can picture. It does so for every tribe in this chapter.

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י לָהֶ֖ם בְּנַֽחֲלָתָ֑ם בְּאֵֽר־שֶׁ֥בַע וְשֶׁ֖בַע וּמוֹלָדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And was for them in their inheritance Beer-sheba and Sheba and Moladah,
pieces: Their inheritance included Beersheba, Sheba, Moladah,

L.2: And there was for them in their inheritance Beersheba, and Sheba, and Moladah,

R.2: Their land included Beersheba, Sheba, Moladah,

decisions.choice: Sheba: kept as in the Hebrew text, though it may repeat the end of the name before it
decisions.reason: With Sheba the list in verses 2-6 has fourteen names, but verse 6 counts thirteen. The same list in 1 Chronicles 4:28 has "Beersheba, Moladah" with no Sheba, and Judah's list has Shema next to Moladah (15:26). Sheba may be a copyist's repeat of the second half of "Beersheba", or another name for Shema. The "and" before it can also be read as "that is", making Sheba a short name for Beersheba itself. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: Beersheba: the chief town of the far south
decisions.reason: Beersheba was linked with Abraham and Isaac (Genesis 21:31-33; 26:23-33) and marked the southern limit of Israel in the saying "from Dan to Beersheba" (Judges 20:1).

decisions.choice: included
decisions.reason: The Hebrew opens the list with "and there was for them in their inheritance". Balanced and Readable say "included". The list runs on to verse 6, so each of these verses ends with a comma.

pieces: Hazar-shual, Balah, Ezem,

L.3: and Hazar-shual, and Balah, and Ezem,

decisions.choice: towns already named in Judah's list
decisions.reason: These three also appear among Judah's southern towns (15:28-29). Balah is spelled Baalah there and Bilhah in 1 Chronicles 4:29; the forms name the same place.

records.source: וְאֶלְתּוֹלַ֥ד וּבְת֖וּל וְחָרְמָֽה׃
records.gloss: and Eltolad and Bethul and Hormah,
pieces: Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah,

L.4: and Eltolad, and Bethul, and Hormah,

decisions.choice: Bethul and Hormah
decisions.reason: Bethul is called Chesil in Judah's list (15:30) and Bethuel in 1 Chronicles 4:30. Hormah got its name from the defeat of the Canaanites there (Numbers 21:3); the name sounds like the word for "devoted to destruction".

pieces: Ziklag, Beth-marcaboth, Hazar-susah,

L.5: and Ziklag, and Beth-marcaboth, and Hazar-susah,

decisions.choice: Ziklag; Beth-marcaboth and Hazar-susah
decisions.reason: Ziklag was later given to David by the Philistine king of Gath (1 Samuel 27:6). Beth-marcaboth means "house of chariots" and Hazar-susah "village of horses"; in the places where Judah's list has Madmannah and Sansannah (15:31), and they may be other names for the same towns.

records.source: וּבֵ֥ית לְבָא֖וֹת וְשָֽׁרוּחֶ֑ן עָרִ֥ים שְׁלֹשׁ־עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה וְחַצְרֵיהֶֽן׃
records.gloss: and Beth-lebaoth and Sharuhen: cities thirteen and their villages;
pieces: Beth-lebaoth and Sharuhen: thirteen towns and their villages,

L.6: and Beth-lebaoth, and Sharuhen: thirteen cities and their villages,

R.6: Beth-lebaoth and Sharuhen. In all, there were thirteen towns with their villages.

decisions.choice: cities and their villages: towns with the open settlements that belonged to them
decisions.reason: The word for "city" is used for any lasting settlement, from a walled town to a small one, and most of these were small. The "villages" were unwalled settlements, farms and hamlets around a town that depended on it (Leviticus 25:31). "Their villages" means the villages of these towns.

decisions.choice: thirteen: the total of the list
decisions.reason: The count agrees with the list if Sheba is not counted as a separate town (see verse 2).

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "cities", the usual word. Balanced and Readable say "towns", since "city" suggests a large place. The same is done through the chapter.

decisions.choice: In all, there were ... with their villages
decisions.reason: Readable closes the list with a short sentence of its own. It does the same with each total in the chapter.

records.gloss: Ain, Rimmon and Ether and Ashan: cities four and their villages,
pieces: and also Ain, Rimmon, Ether and Ashan: four towns and their villages,

L.7: Ain, Rimmon, and Ether, and Ashan: four cities and their villages,

R.7: It also included Ain, Rimmon, Ether and Ashan. In all, there were four towns with their villages.

decisions.choice: Ain, Rimmon: two towns
decisions.reason: In Nehemiah 11:29 the name appears as one town, En-rimmon. Here the count of four requires two, as also in Judah's list (15:32).

decisions.choice: a second group of towns
decisions.reason: Ether and Ashan are listed with Judah's towns in the western foothills (15:42), so Simeon's towns lay in two areas: the Negev in the south and a smaller group to the north-west.

decisions.choice: and also / It also included
decisions.reason: The Hebrew starts the second list with no joining word. Balanced adds "and also" to tie it to the first list, and Readable starts a new sentence.

records.source: וְכָל־הַֽחֲצֵרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר סְבִיבוֹת֙ הֶֽעָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה עַד־בַּֽעֲלַ֥ת בְּאֵ֖ר רָ֣אמַת נֶ֑גֶב זֹ֗את נַחֲלַ֛ת מַטֵּ֥ה בְנֵֽי־שִׁמְע֖וֹן לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: and all the villages which [were] around the cities the these as far as Baalath-beer, Ramah of [the] Negev. This [was the] inheritance of [the] tribe of [the] sons of Simeon by their clans.
pieces: together with all the villages around these towns, out to Baalath-beer, Ramah of the Negev. This was the inheritance of the tribe of Simeon, clan by clan.

L.8: and all the villages that [were] around these cities, as far as Baalath-beer, Ramah of [the] Negev. This [was] the inheritance of the tribe of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Simeon by their clans.

R.8: It also included all the villages around these towns, as far as Baalath-beer, which is Ramah in the Negev, the dry land in the south. This was the share of land that the tribe of Simeon received, clan by clan.

decisions.choice: Baalath-beer, Ramah of the Negev: two names for one place
decisions.reason: The second name explains the first. "Ramah" means "height". The place may be the Ramoth of the Negev to which David sent gifts (1 Samuel 30:27). It marks the farthest point of Simeon's villages.

decisions.choice: the Negev: the dry country of the south
decisions.reason: The Negev is the dry land south of the hill country of Judah, around Beersheba, where rain is scarce and towns stand by wells.

decisions.choice: This was the inheritance ...: the closing words for each tribe
decisions.reason: Each tribe's section ends with this summary (verses 16, 23, 31, 39, 48).

decisions.choice: which is ...; the dry land in the south
decisions.reason: Readable says that the two names are one place and explains the Negev, as the meaning decisions describe.

records.source: מֵחֶ֨בֶל֙ בְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה נַחֲלַ֖ת בְּנֵ֣י שִׁמְע֑וֹן כִּֽי־הָיָ֞ה חֵ֤לֶק בְּנֵֽי־יְהוּדָה֙ רַ֣ב מֵהֶ֔ם וַיִּנְחֲל֥וּ בְנֵֽי־שִׁמְע֖וֹן בְּת֥וֹךְ נַחֲלָתָֽם׃פ
records.gloss: From [the] portion of [the] sons of Judah [was the] inheritance of [the] sons of Simeon, for was [the] portion of [the] sons of Judah too great for them; and received inheritance [the] sons of Simeon in [the] midst of their inheritance.
pieces: The inheritance of the tribe of Simeon came out of the share of the tribe of Judah, because Judah's share was too large for them. So the tribe of Simeon received its inheritance inside Judah's.

L.9: From the portion of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah [was] the inheritance of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Simeon, for the portion of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah was too great for them, and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Simeon received an inheritance in the midst of their inheritance.

R.9: The land of Simeon was taken from Judah's share, because Judah had more land than it needed. So the tribe of Simeon received land inside the land of Judah.

decisions.choice: portion: the part measured out
decisions.reason: This is a different word from "inheritance". It means a share or part that has been measured out, here the land first marked out for Judah (15:1-63).

decisions.choice: too great for them; their inheritance: Judah's
decisions.reason: "Them" and "their" are the people of Judah: their land was more than they could fill and hold, so part of it went to Simeon. Judah's share was the largest of all (chapter 15).

decisions.choice: more land than it needed
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "too great for them" means.

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַל֙ הַגּוֹרָ֣ל הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י לִבְנֵ֥י זְבוּלֻ֖ן לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֑ם וַיְהִ֛י גְּב֥וּל נַחֲלָתָ֖ם עַד־שָׂרִֽיד׃
records.gloss: And came up the lot the third for [the] sons of Zebulun by their clans; and was [the] border of their inheritance as far as Sarid.
pieces: The third lot came up for the tribe of Zebulun, clan by clan. The border of their inheritance reached as far as Sarid.

L.10: And the third lot came up for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Zebulun by their clans. And the border of their inheritance was as far as Sarid.

R.10: The third lot was drawn for the tribe of Zebulun, clan by clan. Their border reached as far as Sarid.

decisions.choice: came up: the lot was drawn out
decisions.reason: Lots were drawn from a container or the fold of a garment, so a lot could be said to "come up" or "come out" (verse 1; Leviticus 16:9). The two verbs describe the same act.

decisions.choice: Zebulun's land and its starting point, Sarid
decisions.reason: Zebulun lay in the hills of lower Galilee, north of the Jezreel Valley, between Asher on the west and Naphtali on the east. Sarid, whose site is not certain, was on its southern edge; from there the border is traced first west (verse 11) and then east (verse 12).

decisions.choice: the tribe of Zebulun, clan by clan
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

records.heading: The land of Zebulun

records.source: וְעָלָ֨ה גְבוּלָ֧ם׀לַיָּ֛מָּה וּמַרְעֲלָ֖ה וּפָגַ֣ע בְּדַבָּ֑שֶׁת וּפָגַע֙ אֶל־הַנַּ֔חַל אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י יָקְנְעָֽם׃
records.gloss: And goes up their border westward and Maralah, and touches on Dabbesheth, and touches to the wadi which [is] on [the] face of Jokneam.
pieces: Their border goes up westward to Maralah, reaches Dabbesheth, and reaches the wadi that faces Jokneam.

L.11: And their border goes up westward, and [to] Maralah, and touches Dabbesheth, and touches the wadi that [is] opposite Jokneam.

R.11: Their border went up to the west, to Maralah. It reached Dabbesheth and the stream valley near Jokneam.

decisions.choice: westward and Maralah: westward, as far as Maralah
decisions.reason: The "and" joins the direction to the place the line reaches; the border climbed westward to Maralah.

decisions.choice: wadi: a stream bed that fills in the rainy season
decisions.reason: The word names a valley cut by a stream that runs with water in the winter rains and may be dry in summer. Jokneam, whose king Joshua defeated (12:22), stood where the hills of Carmel meet the Jezreel Valley.

decisions.choice: on the face of: facing, opposite
decisions.reason: The phrase means "in front of" or "facing", and it can also mean "east of".

decisions.choice: touches / reaches (L, B), reached (R); wadi / stream valley
decisions.reason: The verb means "to meet" or "touch". Literal keeps "touches"; Balanced and Readable say "reaches", which is how a border meets a place. Literal and Balanced keep "wadi", the name for such a valley; Readable says "stream valley". Literal and Balanced trace the line in the present tense and Readable in the past, as in 15:3. The same wording is used through the chapter.

records.source: וְשָׁ֣ב מִשָּׂרִ֗יד קֵ֚דְמָה מִזְרַ֣ח הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ עַל־גְּב֥וּל כִּסְלֹ֖ת תָּבֹ֑ר וְיָצָ֥א אֶל־הַדָּֽבְרַ֖ת וְעָלָ֥ה יָפִֽיעַ׃
records.gloss: And turns back from Sarid eastward, toward [the] rising of the sun, to [the] border of Chisloth-tabor, and goes out to Daberath, and goes up [to] Japhia.
pieces: From Sarid it turns east, toward the sunrise, to the border of Chisloth-tabor, goes on to Daberath, and goes up to Japhia.

L.12: And it turns from Sarid eastward, toward the sunrise, to the border of Chisloth-tabor, and goes out to Daberath, and goes up to Japhia.

R.12: From Sarid the border also went east to the edge of Chisloth-tabor. It went on to Daberath and up to Japhia.

decisions.choice: turned from Sarid eastward: the line traced the other way from its starting point
decisions.reason: Verse 11 took the border west from Sarid; now it is traced east from the same point along the south side of Zebulun's land.

decisions.choice: Chisloth-tabor and Daberath, near Mount Tabor
decisions.reason: Chisloth-tabor ("slopes of Tabor") is probably the Chesulloth of Issachar's list (verse 18). Daberath, at the foot of Mount Tabor, was later given to the Levites from Issachar (21:28).

decisions.choice: leaves out "toward the sunrise"
decisions.reason: Readable gives the direction once, as "east", since "toward the sunrise" repeats it. It does the same in verse 13.

records.source: וּמִשָּׁ֤ם עָבַר֙ קֵ֣דְמָה מִזְרָ֔חָה גִּתָּ֥ה חֵ֖פֶר עִתָּ֣ה קָצִ֑ין וְיָצָ֛א רִמּ֥וֹן הַמְּתֹאָ֖ר הַנֵּעָֽה׃
records.gloss: And from there passes on eastward, toward sunrise, to Gath-hepher, to Eth-kazin; and goes out [to] Rimmon, the bending to Neah.
pieces: From there it goes on east, toward the sunrise, to Gath-hepher and Eth-kazin, and goes out to Rimmon, where it bends toward Neah.

L.13: And from there it passes along eastward, toward the sunrise, to Gath-hepher, to Eth-kazin, and goes out to Rimmon, which bends toward Neah.

R.13: From there it went on east to Gath-hepher and Eth-kazin. Then it went to Rimmon and turned toward Neah.

decisions.choice: Rimmon, which bends toward Neah: the border bends at Rimmon
decisions.reason: The word after Rimmon is a form of a verb meaning "to be marked out" or "to stretch". It most likely tells how the border runs: from Rimmon it turns toward Neah. It has also been read as part of a longer place name.

decisions.choice: Gath-hepher: the home town of Jonah
decisions.reason: The prophet Jonah son of Amittai came from Gath-hepher (2 Kings 14:25).

records.source: וְנָסַ֤ב אֹתוֹ֙ הַגְּב֔וּל מִצְּפ֖וֹן חַנָּתֹ֑ן וְהָיוּ֙ תֹּֽצְאֹתָ֔יו גֵּ֖י יִפְתַּח־אֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And turns around it the border on [the] north [to] Hannathon; and were its ends [the] valley of Iphtah-el.
pieces: On the north the border goes around to Hannathon and ends at the valley of Iphtah-el.

L.14: And the border goes around it on the north to Hannathon, and its end is at the valley of Iphtah-el.

R.14: On the north side, the border went around to Hannathon and ended at the valley of Iphtah-el.

decisions.choice: goes around it: around the territory
decisions.reason: "It" is most likely Zebulun's land: the line now curves round from the east side to the north.

decisions.choice: its ends: where the border line runs out
decisions.reason: The word names the end point of a border line. It closes the lines in verses 22, 29 and 33 as well.

decisions.choice: the valley of Iphtah-el: where Zebulun met Asher
decisions.reason: Asher's border also reaches this valley (verse 27), so it marked the meeting point of the two tribes on the north-west.

decisions.choice: its end is at (L); ends at (B); ended at (R)
decisions.reason: For "its ends were", Literal says "its end is at", as in Numbers 34:5 and 15:4; Balanced says "ends at" and Readable "ended at", here and through the chapter.

records.source: וְקַטָּ֤ת וְנַֽהֲלָל֙ וְשִׁמְר֔וֹן וְיִדְאֲלָ֖ה וּבֵ֣ית לָ֑חֶם עָרִ֥ים שְׁתֵּים־עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה וְחַצְרֵיהֶֽן׃
records.gloss: And Kattath and Nahalal and Shimron and Idalah and Bethlehem: cities twelve and their villages.
pieces: Also in it were Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah and Bethlehem: twelve towns and their villages.

L.15: And Kattath, and Nahalal, and Shimron, and Idalah, and Bethlehem: twelve cities and their villages.

R.15: Its land also included Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah and Bethlehem. In all, there were twelve towns with their villages.

decisions.choice: twelve: a total that includes towns already named along the border
decisions.reason: Only five towns are named here. The total most likely counts towns named in the border too, such as Japhia, Daberath and Rimmon, but exactly which ones is no longer certain. The same is true of the totals in verses 22, 30 and 38.

decisions.choice: Bethlehem: a town of Zebulun, not the Bethlehem of Judah
decisions.reason: This is a second town of the same name, in Galilee, west of Nazareth. The Bethlehem of Ruth and David lies south of Jerusalem (Ruth 1:1; Micah 5:1).

decisions.choice: Also in it were / Its land also included
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds the names with a plain "and". Balanced and Readable add a few words so the list reads as a sentence.

R.16: This was the share of land that the tribe of Zebulun received, clan by clan: these towns and their villages.

decisions.choice: the closing words of the tribe's section
decisions.reason: As in verse 8: the summary that ends each tribe's allotment.

decisions.choice: the tribe of Zebulun; share of land
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

L.17: For Issachar the fourth lot came out, for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Issachar by their clans.

records.gloss: And went out [the] territory of [the] sons of Dan from them; and went up [the] sons of Dan and fought with Leshem, and captured it and struck it to [the] mouth of [the] sword, and took possession of it and lived in it; and called Leshem Dan, according to [the] name of Dan their father.
pieces: But the territory of the Danites was lost to them, so the Danites went up and fought against Leshem. They captured it, put it to the sword, took possession of it, and settled there. They renamed Leshem Dan, after their ancestor Dan.

L.47: And the territory of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Dan went out from them. And the sons of Dan went up and fought against Leshem, and captured it, and struck it with the mouth of the sword, and took possession of it, and lived in it; and they called Leshem Dan, after the name of Dan their father.

R.47: But the tribe of Dan lost control of its land. So the Danites went north and attacked the town of Leshem. They captured it and killed its people with their swords. Then they took it over and settled there. They named it Dan, after Dan, the father of their tribe.

decisions.choice: the territory went out from them: the land slipped out of their control
alternatives: the territory of the Danites went out beyond these towns
decisions.reason: The words most likely mean that Dan's land was lost to them, as Judges 1:34 tells: the Amorites forced the Danites into the hills and kept them from the plain. They can also mean that the territory reached out beyond the towns just listed. The ancient Greek translation reads differently again, saying that the Danites did not drive out the Amorites who pressed them. This note is from general knowledge of the Greek translation and should be checked by a reviewer.

decisions.choice: Leshem renamed Dan: the story of Judges 18
decisions.reason: Leshem is the Laish of Judges 18, a quiet town far to the north near the springs of the Jordan. Judges 18 tells how the Danites sent spies, attacked it and renamed it Dan. This note looks ahead to events after the time of the allotments; the town later marks Israel's northern limit, "from Dan to Beersheba" (Judges 20:1).

decisions.choice: struck it to the mouth of the sword: killed its people with the sword
decisions.reason: The sword is pictured as a mouth that devours (Deuteronomy 32:42). "Struck it" means the town's people (Judges 18:27).

decisions.choice: Dan their father: Jacob's son, the tribe's ancestor
decisions.reason: Dan was the son of Jacob and Bilhah (Genesis 30:6), from whom the tribe was descended.

decisions.choice: the sons of Dan / the Danites
decisions.reason: Literal gives the first "sons of Dan", the tribe whose land it was, with the gender setting; the second names the men who went to war, so it has no setting. Balanced and Readable say "the Danites" for both.

decisions.choice: went north
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "went up". Readable says "went north", since Leshem lay in the far north (Judges 18:7, 29), and "killed its people" for "struck it".

decisions.choice: dividing for inheritance: handing out the land as lasting possessions
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the same root as "inheritance". It means to give out land as property that each tribe and family would keep.

decisions.choice: Joshua receives his share last
decisions.reason: The leader is given his own land only after every tribe has received its share. Caleb, the other faithful spy, had also received his land by promise (14:6-15).

decisions.choice: When they had finished ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the first clause a time clause, since the gift to Joshua comes after the division is done.

records.source: עַל־פִּ֨י יְהוָ֜ה נָ֣תְנוּ ל֗וֹ אֶת־הָעִיר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁאָ֔ל אֶת־תִּמְנַת־סֶ֖רַח בְּהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיִּבְנֶ֥ה אֶת־הָעִ֖יר וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: At [the] mouth of Yahweh they gave to him the city which he asked, Timnath-serah in [the] hill country of Ephraim; and he built the city and lived in it.
pieces: At the command of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} they gave him the town he asked for, Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim. He built up the town and settled there.

L.50: At the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} they gave him the city that he asked for, Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim, and he built the city and lived in it.

R.50: As {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded, they gave him the town he asked for. It was Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim. Joshua built up the town and lived there.

decisions.choice: at the mouth of the LORD: by the LORD's command
decisions.reason: "Mouth" stands for what someone says. The phrase means "at the LORD's word" or "by his order" (Numbers 3:16; 9:18). The command itself is not recorded; Joshua, like Caleb, had been promised that he would enter the land (Numbers 14:30).

decisions.choice: Timnath-serah in Ephraim
decisions.reason: Joshua belonged to the tribe of Ephraim (Numbers 13:8). He was buried in this town (24:30), which Judges 2:9 calls Timnath-heres.

decisions.choice: built: rebuilt or strengthened
decisions.reason: The verb can mean building a town anew or building up one that already stood, by repairing and fortifying it.

decisions.choice: built up
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "built up", which fits either sense; Literal keeps "built".

pieces: Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the family heads of the tribes of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} handed out these inheritances by lot at Shiloh, before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the entrance of the tent of meeting. So they finished dividing the land.

L.51: These [are] the inheritances that Eleazar the priest, and Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel gave as possessions by lot in Shiloh before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, at the entrance of the tent of meeting. And they finished dividing the land.

R.51: Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun and the family leaders of the tribes of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} gave out these shares of land. They drew lots at Shiloh, in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the entrance of the meeting tent. So they finished dividing up the land.

decisions.choice: Eleazar, Joshua and the family heads: the leaders named for this task
decisions.reason: The LORD had named these leaders to divide the land: Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and one leader from each tribe (Numbers 34:16-29). The same group is named when the dividing begins (14:1).

decisions.choice: at Shiloh, before the LORD, at the tent of meeting
decisions.reason: The tent of meeting had been set up at Shiloh (18:1). To cast lots "before the LORD" at its entrance was to leave the outcome to him in his presence (18:6, 8, 10).

decisions.choice: the heads of the fathers: the heads of the ancestral families
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the family lines within a tribe; their heads were the tribe's leaders (Numbers 32:28).

decisions.choice: and they finished dividing the land: the close of the whole division
decisions.reason: The words repeat the start of verse 49 and close the account of the dividing of the land that began in 14:1.

decisions.choice: family heads / family leaders
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "families" for "fathers", following the meaning decision; Literal keeps "fathers".
